bounded_hypothesis: Conditional on the MD5-verified public Zenodo 8223844 SMAG archive-order genome pool (recalled with Pyrodigal v3.7.1 -p meta --no-stop-codon) and the staged 52,515 published GEM Prodigal proteomes, after canonicalizing sequences (stripping trailing '*'), deduplicating within each reference arm, applying an explicit cross-release overlap rule, and enforcing exact common-support matching of unique reference protein counts across protein length strata, does the SMAG reference subset yield a different paired hit rate than length- and count-matched GEM reference subsets for Empty Quarter dark protein families under identical DIAMOND blastp settings?
critical_issues: Unmatched reference protein length distributions and un-deduplicated pools: Despite DOSSIER.md:1,29,68 and DESIGN.md:24,41-42 claiming length-matched reference comparison, scripts/06_match_gem_and_search.py:68-98 only samples whole GEM proteomes until raw protein count reaches >=693,227 (694,598 GEM vs 693,227 SMAG). GEM has +9.28% more characters, higher mean/median length (319.20/271.00 aa vs 292.68/252.00 aa), 15.1x higher internal duplicate rate (2.26% vs 0.15%, leaving 678,867 canonical unique GEM proteins vs 692,194 in SMAG), and major reference length-stratum imbalances (+16.8% more <100 aa and +12.3% more 100-149 aa targets in SMAG; +17.5% more >=400 aa targets in GEM). Repair: deduplicate canonical sequences first and enforce exact common-support quota matching of unique reference proteins across length strata across repeated deterministic GEM draws, then re-run DIAMOND makedb/blastp.

Uncanonicalized trailing stop codons ('*') between callers: scripts/05_extract_and_genecall_smag.py:31 calls SMAG with --no-stop-codon (0/693,227 trailing '*'), whereas scripts/06_match_gem_and_search.py:81-90 retains published GEM trailing '*' on 663,757/694,598 (95.56%) proteins. Neither read_fasta_stats (line 37) nor hash_fasta (lines 103-120) strips '*', inflating GEM residue count by +663,757, shifting complete GEM protein lengths by +1 aa, and forcing exact MD5 overlap for complete proteins to 0 (reported as 0.00% in results/smag_vs_gem_redundancy_overlap_audit.tsv:9-10 and DOSSIER.md:70,129, whereas canonicalized rstrip('*').upper() sequences share 30 exact matches). Repair: strip trailing '*' and uppercase all sequences on ingestion before length, redundancy, and cross-catalogue overlap audits and database construction; also fix '32-mer MD5' terminology in DOSSIER.md:69,127.

Unsafe partial tar extraction, non-deterministic FASTA ordering, and deleted unhashed source genomes: Contradicting DESIGN.md:59-61 (which claims Python tarfile member.size verification), scripts/05_extract_and_genecall_smag.py:84 runs 'cat ... | tar -xz ... 2>/dev/null || true' and lines 100-120 check only size>=1000, leading '>', and trailing newline (which cannot detect multi-contig truncation at line boundaries). Job 53704317 (logs/pilot_v2_53704317.out:11-13) skipped extraction entirely via line 81 ('if not extracted_files:'), reusing 212 pre-extracted files, then lines 169-171 deleted all 212 nucleotide FASTA files without SHA-256 hashes or declared/observed byte records in results/smag_pilot_genome_manifest.tsv. Line 140-145 writes smag_pilot_recalled.faa in non-deterministic ProcessPoolExecutor as_completed order. Repair: stream verified archive parts via Python tarfile (mode='r|gz'), enforce len(data)==member.size (explicitly logging rejected 213th member MAG/SRR5855438rbin.1.fa at 6,995,968/12,783,848 bytes), retain extracted genomes with SHA-256 checksums in the manifest, and sort records deterministically before writing smag_pilot_recalled.faa.

Missing GEM manifest/checksums, hit-definition mismatch, unweighted equal-quota query pooling, and overstated full-test claims: scripts/06_match_gem_and_search.py:76-95 never saves sampled_gem_files (292 GEM genome IDs), and INPUTS.tsv:17,22-23 leaves GEM directory and both searched pilot FASTAs (234 MB and 322 MB) without SHA-256 hashes ('uncomputed_large'). DOSSIER.md:39 defines hits as E<=1e-3 and >=30% identity, but 06_match_gem_and_search.py:160-179 applies no pident>=30% filter (28/1,089 SMAG and 21/926 GEM hits have pident<30%). Equal-quota query strata (200/bin in 02_sample_queries.py:64-83) are summed unweighted in 06_match_gem_and_search.py:193-214 and pooled across dark+ctrl ('all'), and 0/0 is written as 'inf' in results/smag_vs_gem_matched_length_stratified.tsv:11. DOSSIER.md:203-210 (§8) claims causal soil-biome and caller-independent conclusions that the design cannot identify. Repair: write a complete GEM subset manifest and all FASTA SHA-256 hashes, reconcile the pident>=30% hit rule, report stratum-specific and population-weighted (or full 212,084-query) estimates without pooling dark+ctrl, fix 0/0 formatting, and restrict §7-8 to bounded caller-conditional reference-release comparisons.
optional_improvements: Full-catalogue Zenodo 8223844 download (all 373 parts, ~39 GB) to extend the SMAG pool beyond the archive-order pilot parts.
External nucleotide assembly download for GEM MAGs to re-call GEM with Pyrodigal v3.7.1 for a fully caller-harmonized sensitivity analysis.
Three-arm GEM metadata stratification (Soil vs Non-Soil) and MMseqs2 95%/50% sequence clustering across full catalogues.
scope_changes_from_original: Narrowed from a full-catalogue, caller-harmonized soil-biome effect (round5/EXTENSIONS.md H3) to a bounded reference-release subset comparison conditioned on the MD5-verified public Zenodo SMAG archive-order genome pool (recalled with Pyrodigal v3.7.1) and published GEM Prodigal proteomes.
Removed v1 claims that annotated control families calibrate the quantitative share of technical vs biological discordance or isolate residual desert lineage adaptation.
reason: h3_v2 empirically proves top-1 post-hoc subsampling bias (Job 53700569) and demonstrates public Zenodo SMAG ingestion and paired DIAMOND blastp execution (Job 53704317), but fails to implement the claimed reference length-stratum matching and sequence deduplication, omits trailing '*' stop-codon canonicalization between Pyrodigal and GEM Prodigal (falsifying the 0.00% overlap audit), uses partial shell tar extraction without header byte-size verification while deleting unhashed source genomes, and omits GEM genome manifests and FASTA checksums.
